selected_mechanism.name: NMFS MMPA IHA Cook Inlet Natural Gas Production Authorization

news_trigger.what_happened: Takes of Marine Mammals Incidental to Specified Activities; Taking Marine Mammals Incidental to HEX Operating, LLC Natural Gas Activities in Cook Inlet, Alaska. NMFS issued a one-year renewal Incidental Harassment Authorization allowing HEX Operating, LLC (formerly Furie Operating Alaska, LLC) to incidentally harass marine mammals incidental to natural gas activities in Cook Inlet, Alaska, specifically relocating the Enterprise 151 jack-up production rig to the Allegra Lee Platform through rig towing activities. Signed June 16, 2026 by Kimberly Damon-Randall, Director, Office of Protected Resources. Effective September 13, 2026 through September 12, 2027.

selected_mechanism.one_line_definition: Under MMPA Section 101(a)(5)(D), NMFS's Office of Protected Resources Director issues or denies annual Incidental Harassment Authorizations that are the sole legal permission allowing Cook Inlet natural gas operators to conduct production activities, without which platforms go offline and the gas supply underpinning Southcentral Alaska's Railbelt electricity grid is curtailed. The IHA is a single-signature authorization that no other agency or body can substitute.

layers.name: MMPA Statutory Authority
layers.what_it_does: Establishes that any U.S. citizen engaged in a specified activity other than commercial fishing that may incidentally take small numbers of marine mammals must obtain prior authorization from NMFS under Section 101(a)(5)(A) or (D). Without statutory compliance, Cook Inlet production activities are illegal regardless of state permits or leases.
layers.controlling_actor: U.S. Congress (enacted authority); administered by NMFS under Department of Commerce

primary_source.outlet: GovInfo / Federal Register cites 16 U.S.C. 1361 et seq. (MMPA) as authority

layers.name: Applicant Layer HEX Operating LLC Application
layers.what_it_does: HEX Operating, LLC (formerly Furie Operating Alaska, LLC), the Cook Inlet gas producer, must apply annually to NMFS OPR for renewal of its IHA, providing activity descriptions, take estimates, and mitigation plans. The application defines the scope of what is authorized. If HEX does not apply or NMFS does not renew, the rig relocation enabling production access is blocked.
layers.controlling_actor: HEX Operating, LLC, Cook Inlet natural gas producer operating the Allegra Lee Platform and Enterprise 151 jack-up rig

primary_source.outlet: GovInfo / Federal Register 2026-12463 names HEX Operating LLC and describes the rig towing activities authorized

layers.name: ESA Section 7 Biological Opinion NMFS Alaska Regional
layers.what_it_does: Before the IHA can be issued, NMFS must complete an ESA Section 7 consultation to ensure the authorized activity will not jeopardize endangered species (Cook Inlet beluga whales are listed). The Alaska Regional Office issues a Biological Opinion that is a prerequisite gate within the MMPA authorization process. An adverse BiOp or jeopardy finding blocks IHA issuance.
layers.controlling_actor: NMFS Alaska Regional Office, conducts ESA Section 7 consultation

primary_source.outlet: NOAA Fisheries, Office of Protected Resources page establishing OPR authority over MMPA/ESA coordination

layers.name: OPR Director IHA Issuance Asymmetric Chokepoint
layers.what_it_does: The Director of NMFS Office of Protected Resources issues or denies the IHA by individual signature. No committee vote, no co-signature, no external ratification is required. The IHA signed by Kimberly Damon-Randall on June 16, 2026 is the single document that legally permits HEX Operating to conduct rig towing in Cook Inlet for the September 2026 to September 2027 production season. Denial or non-renewal halts Cook Inlet gas production activities.
layers.controlling_actor: Kimberly Damon-Randall, Director, NMFS Office of Protected Resources, sole signing authority confirmed in FR document

primary_source.outlet: GovInfo / Federal Register 2026-12463 signature block names Kimberly Damon-Randall, Director, Office of Protected Resources, National Marine Fisheries Service

layers.name: Cook Inlet Gas to Railbelt Power to Southcentral Alaska Electricity Supply
layers.what_it_does: Cook Inlet natural gas is the primary fuel for gas-fired power generation serving the Railbelt grid (Anchorage, Kenai Peninsula, Mat-Su), which supplies electricity to all proposed AI data center sites in Southcentral Alaska. Cook Inlet gas production constraints directly cap available power for large AI loads. Chugach Electric Association's June 2026 LOI with Glenfarne for Alaska LNG pipeline gas supply signals current Cook Inlet gas dependence and forward supply risk.
layers.controlling_actor: Chugach Electric Association (largest Railbelt utility, gas-fired generation operator) and other Railbelt utilities

primary_source.outlet: Chugach Electric Association homepage June 2026 news item on Glenfarne LOI for natural gas from Alaska LNG pipeline confirming current Cook Inlet gas dependence

selected_mechanism.chokepoint: Layer 4, OPR Director IHA issuance. Kimberly Damon-Randall (Director, NMFS Office of Protected Resources) holds genuine unilateral signing authority over the annual IHA renewal. She is the single institutional role whose signature is the rate-limiting step. Without the signed IHA, HEX Operating cannot legally conduct rig towing or platform operations in Cook Inlet, cannot produce gas, and the binary she owns is issue versus deny or delay, with no committee override, no co-signer, no substitute authorization pathway available under MMPA for this class of activity.
selected_mechanism.ak_consequence: Cook Inlet gas sector (HEX Operating, Allegra Lee Platform). If the FY2027 IHA renewal effective September 13, 2026 is denied, conditioned, or delayed by the OPR Director, Cook Inlet gas production from the Allegra Lee Platform ceases, tightening the Railbelt gas supply that Chugach Electric and other Southcentral Alaska utilities depend on for gas-fired generation, directly constraining the power supply available to proposed AI data center projects (STAK 1 to 3 GW, DigitalBridge Southcentral sites) by Q4 2026.
selected_mechanism.structural_read: The HEX IHA mechanism is the upstream gas-production permitting chokepoint for Southcentral Alaska's power supply. Every proposed AI data center in the Anchorage, Kenai, and Mat-Su corridor depends on Railbelt electricity. Railbelt electricity is majority gas-fired. Cook Inlet gas is the primary fuel source. And Cook Inlet production rights are gated annually by a single NMFS OPR Director signature under MMPA. The mechanism is not about environmental politics. It is about the administrative annual renewal cycle that silently governs whether Cook Inlet gas production can physically continue each operating season. Chugach's June 2026 LOI with Glenfarne for future LNG pipeline gas is an acknowledgment that this annual NMFS gate is a long-term structural vulnerability. The utilities are already seeking supply diversification precisely because the Cook Inlet IHA renewal cycle is a chokepoint they cannot control.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: Any AI data center developer (STAK, DigitalBridge, or a hyperscale anchor tenant) pursuing a Southcentral Alaska site should obtain from Chugach Electric written confirmation that their power supply contract is not contingent on Cook Inlet gas production from platforms requiring MMPA IHAs, and should assess whether the September 13, 2026 effective date of the HEX IHA creates a Q3 to Q4 2026 gas-supply gap that would affect construction-phase power procurement timelines.
